classification.difficultyReason: Read labelled intersections and parallel markings, and express parallel relationships symbolically.

content.prompt: The second diagram to the right shows two pairs of parallel lines.

spec.description: Four extended lines with labelled intersections. Single parallel arrows mark the two rising lines; double parallel arrows mark the two steep lines. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: A and B lie on the lower rising line; D and C lie on the upper rising line. A and D lie on the left steep line; B and C lie on the right steep line. AB is parallel to DC and AD is parallel to BC.
spec.answerVisibility: All lines, labels and parallel markings are permanent question givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In symbols, write ‘$AB$ is parallel to $DC$’.

answer.worked: $AB\parallel DC$. The symbol $\parallel$ means ‘is parallel to’.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In symbols, write ‘$BC$ is parallel to $AD$’.

answer.worked: $BC\parallel AD$. The matching double arrow markings identify these parallel lines.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the intersection of the lines $AB$ and $BC$?

children.label: d
children.prompt: What point lies on both $BC$ and $CD$?

answer.worked: The point $C$ is the intersection of $BC$ and $CD$, so it lies on both lines.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Do any points lie on both lines $AB$ and $CD$?

answer.short: No, the two lines are parallel.
answer.worked: No. The matching single arrow markings show that $AB\parallel CD$. Parallel lines never meet, so they have no point in common.
